questions.q: Whom did the messenger help and protect during the first year that Darius the Mede was king?
questions.a: The messenger helped and protected Michael that year.

questions.q: How will a fourth king in Persia gain power?
questions.a: He will gain power through his riches.

questions.q: Against what kingdom will that fourth Persian king stir up everyone?
questions.a: He will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Javan.

questions.q: What will a mighty king do when he rises to power?
questions.a: He will rule with great dominion and do whatever he wants.

questions.q: To whom will the kingdom of the mighty king not be given?
questions.a: That kingdom will not be given to the king’s own descendants.

questions.q: Who will make an alliance?
questions.a: The king of the south and one of his commanders who will become a king of the north will make an alliance.

questions.q: Who will come to confirm the alliance between the king of the south and the king of the north?
questions.a: The daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to confirm the agreement.

questions.q: What will the branch from the daughter of the king of the south do to the king of the north?
questions.a: He will attack the army and enter the fortress of the king of the north and conquer them.

questions.q: What will the king of the south take back to Egypt?
questions.a: He will take the idols, metal images, and silver and gold treasures of the north to Egypt.

questions.q: What will happen when the king of the north invades the southern kingdom?
questions.a: He will have to retreat back to his own land.

questions.q: What will the sons of the king of the north do?
questions.a: They will wage war and assemble a great army. They will overflow like a flood, pass through, and repeat the assault all the way to the fortress of the king of the south.

questions.q: Who will win this battle between the north and the south?
questions.a: The king of the south will win that battle.

questions.q: What will the king of the south do in response to the attack by the sons of the king of the north?
questions.a: The king of the south will march out in a rage and fight against the king of the north.

questions.q: After some years, what will the king of the north do?
questions.a: He will raise another great army supplied with much equipment and will surely come.

questions.q: In those times who else will rise against the king of the south?
questions.a: In those times many will rise against the king of the south, including the most violent among Daniel’s people.

questions.q: What will happen this time when the king of the north attacks the king of the south?
questions.a: The king of the south will not be able to stand against him. The king of the north will do whatever he wants against the king of the south.

questions.q: Why will the king of the north give a daughter in marriage to the king of the south?
questions.a: The king of the north will do this in order to destroy the kingdom of the south.

questions.q: What will happen to this king of the North?
questions.a: A commander will defeat him and shame him, instead of being shamed himself. Then he will retreat to the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and die, and no one will find him.

questions.q: What will the one who rises up in place of the king of the north do?
questions.a: He will force taxes to be paid to provide for the splendor of the kingdom.

questions.q: What will happen to this one who forces taxes to be paid?
questions.a: After only a few days that one will be destroyed, but not in anger or in battle.

questions.q: How will a despised person who has not been given the honor of royalty come to power?
questions.a: He will come to power quietly, when people are not expecting it, and will take over the kingdom by making secret plots.

questions.q: Whom will the despised king also remove, besides defeating the armies opposing him?
questions.a: He will also remove God’s high priest, the leader of the covenant.

questions.q: What will this despised king do once an alliance is made with him?
questions.a: From the time an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully.

questions.q: What will the king do with the plunder he takes from the richest parts of the province?
questions.a: He will give the plunder, spoil, and wealth to his troops and supporters.

questions.q: What will happen when this deceitful king wages war against the king of the south?
questions.a: The king of the south will not be able to stand against the deceitful king because of all the plots devised against him.

questions.q: Who will help destroy the king of the south?
questions.a: Some of his own royal officials will help destroy him, and many of his soldiers will be killed.

questions.q: Why will the king of the north and the king of the south sit at the same table and lie to each other?
questions.a: They will lie to each other because their hearts are set on evil against each other.

questions.q: What will the heart of the king of the north be set against?
questions.a: His heart will be set against the holy covenant.

questions.q: What will happen when the king of the north invades the south again at the appointed time?
questions.a: He will invade again, but this time it will not go as it did before.

questions.q: How will the king of the north show his rage against the holy covenant?
questions.a: He will show his rage by favoring those who abandon the holy covenant.

questions.q: What will the king’s army do to the sanctuary?
questions.a: They will make the sanctuary unclean, stop the regular sacrifice, and set up the abomination that makes it desolate.

questions.q: How will the people who know their God respond to the king’s flattery?
questions.a: They will be strong and take action against him.

questions.q: What will happen to the wise?
questions.a: For a time, the wise will fall by the sword and by flame, be taken as prisoners, and be robbed of their possessions. When they stumble, they will receive a little help.

questions.q: What will the wise do at that time?
questions.a: At that time, the wise will give understanding to many.

questions.q: Why will some of the wise stumble?
questions.a: Some of them will stumble so that they may be refined, cleansed, and made pure until the time of the end.

questions.q: Above whom will this deceitful king of the north exalt himself?
questions.a: He will exalt and magnify himself above every god, including the God of gods, the gods of his ancestors, and the god desired by women.

questions.q: What god will the king honor instead of the gods of his fathers?
questions.a: He will honor a god of fortresses that his ancestors did not know, honoring it with gold, silver, precious stones, and other valuable things.

questions.q: What will this deceitful king of the north do for those who acknowledge him?
questions.a: He will give honor to those who acknowledge him. He will make them rulers over many people.

questions.q: What will the king of the north use to attack at the time of the end?
questions.a: He will attack with chariots, horsemen, and many ships, invading many countries.

questions.q: At the time of the end, what will happen when the king of the north comes into the glorious land?
questions.a: Many people in that land will stumble and fall.

questions.q: Who will escape from the hand of the king of the north?
questions.a: Edom, Moab, and most of the people of Ammon will escape from his hand.

questions.q: What are some of the countries over which this king of the north will extend his power?
questions.a: This king of the north will extend his power over Egypt, the Libyans, and the Cushites.

questions.q: What will this king of the north do when reports from the east and north alarm him?
questions.a: He will go out with great rage to destroy and to devote many to destruction.

questions.q: Where will this king of the north set up the tents of his palace?
questions.a: He will set up the tents of his palace between the seas, at the mountain of the beauty of holiness.

questions.q: Who will help the king of the north at the end?
questions.a: The king of the north will come to his end, and there will be no one to help him.

commentary.text: The vision of the Scriptures of truth.

Dan. 11:1-30 The angel shows Daniel the succession of the Persian and Grecian empires. The kings of Egypt and Syria are noticed: Judea was between their dominions, and affected by their contests. From Dan. 11:5-30, is generally considered to relate to the events which came to pass during the continuance of these governments; and from Dan. 11:21, to relate to Antiochus Epiphanes, who was a cruel and violent persecutor of the Jews. See what decaying, perishing things worldly pomp and possessions are, and the power by which they are gotten. God, in his providence, sets up one, and pulls down another, as he pleases. This world is full of wars and fightings, which come from men's lusts. All changes and revolutions of states and kingdoms, and every event, are plainly and perfectly foreseen by God. No word of God shall fall to the ground; but what he has designed, what he has declared, shall infallibly come to pass. While the potsherds of the earth strive with each other, they prevail and are prevailed against, deceive and are deceived; but those who know God will trust in him, and he will enable them to stand their ground, bear their cross, and maintain their conflict.

Dan. 11:31-45 The remainder of this prophecy is very difficult, and commentators differ much respecting it. From Antiochus the account seems to pass to antichrist. Reference seems to be made to the Roman empire, the fourth monarchy, in its pagan, early Christian, and papal states. The end of the Lord's anger against his people approaches, as well as the end of his patience towards his enemies. If we would escape the ruin of the infidel, the idolater, the superstitious and cruel persecutor, as well as that of the profane, let us make the oracles of God our standard of truth and of duty, the foundation of our hope, and the light of our paths through this dark world, to the glorious inheritance above.
